characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five Cu molds moved stepwise inside furnace; successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast remaining melt adjusted by charging Al through an air lock; after cooling and cutting, blocks were 10×50×130 mm³.

processing_steps.reduction_ratio: 10×50×130 mm³ blocks hot rolled into 2±0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: cut into sets of nine segments with dimensions 2×60×55 mm³ for each alloy composition
performed after the heat treatments to remove surface scales

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: average of three measurements for every material state

structures.overall_structure: fully recrystallized single-phase austenitic (fcc) microstructure with grain size ~20 μm and some retained Mn microsegregations; no cracks, pores, or macrosegregations

unmapped_findings: For the Al-free reference material (ternary Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy), the best mechanical behavior is found for the as-homogenized state: 360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS (high work hardening), and 77% TE. Aging leaves the YS virtually unchanged and increases the hardness slightly, but reduces UTS and TE (applies to the aged 450 °C, 1 h condition) [b0023, b0024].
Embrittlement of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy becomes most apparent for long aging times (24 h) and higher temperatures (>500 °C) [b0024].

For the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C reference (0 wt.% Al), a single austenite phase prevails at room temperature and the TWIP effect prevails as the deformation mechanism (dislocation-based strain hardening followed at higher loads by mechanical twinning), classifying it as a SIMPLEX low-density TWIP steel [b0015, b0031].
